questions.question: What is the correct chronological order of the stages of English?
options: Old English, Middle English, Early Modern English, Modern English
Middle English, Old English, Modern English, Early Modern English
Modern English, Middle English, Old English, Early Modern English
Early Modern English, Old English, Middle English, Modern English
questions.explanation: English developed from Old English (450-1100) through Middle English (1100-1500) and Early Modern English (1500-1700) to Modern English (1700-).

questions.question: Which event brought strong French influence into English?
options: The invention of the printing press
questions.explanation: After the Norman invasion in 1066, French became the language of the rulers, bringing thousands of French words into English.

questions.question: In which period of English did Shakespeare write?
questions.explanation: Shakespeare wrote in Early Modern English - recognisable but old-fashioned to us: "To be or not to be, that is the question."

questions.question: Which famous Old English poem begins "Hwat! We Gardena in geardagum..."?
questions.explanation: Beowulf is the famous Old English epic. The Canterbury Tales by Chaucer is Middle English, and Hamlet is Early Modern English.

questions.question: Which of these is a reason why languages change?
options: Contact with other languages, technology and social change
Languages are fixed by law and never change
Old words are randomly deleted every decade
questions.explanation: Languages change through contact with other languages, new technology, social changes and globalisation.
